hook: SCP-557 reads like an archaeology report on an ancient tomb under the Omani desert, one the Foundation could not move and so built a whole site around. The pleasure is in descending level by level and noticing what changes the deeper you go. Watch the dates, and the one door that does not belong to its era.
whyItMatters: It is a good example of an article built around a place rather than a creature. The structure itself tells the story of a containment effort far older than the Foundation, described as an ancient prison with floors set aside for heretics, sorcerers and the abnormal. The final note from its last keeper gives the dry survey a human voice.
thingsToNotice:
The levels form a descending scale: guard quarters and a library on Level 1, cells for heretics and sorcerers that fell out of use long before the end, a floor where skeletons resembling other anomalies lie locked in stone cells, and finally a trapped corridor leading to Room 501. There the door, made of a material that should not exist that early, was torn down from the inside, and the dust puts that event only about twenty years ago. The chains on the standing block are of the same material, and the thing they held, called simply the prisoner and once 'the bastard son of Apep', is nowhere to be found.

That is why the procedures read as they do: the escaped prisoner is to be presumed Keter, and the staff also serve as a strike team for anything that comes up from beneath the rune-covered granite block of roughly 80,000 kg. The Greek note from the last of the Keepers adds the second fear, a gateway to the dark that must stay shut, and says that even the gods could not kill the prisoner.
